title: Diljit Dosanjh and Kangana Ranaut Are About to Clash Again. This Time the Battlefield Is the Box Office.
excerpt: Five years after their public feud over the farmers' protest, Main Vaapas Aaunga and Bharat Bhhagya Viddhaata will open on the same day. For the diaspora, only one of these films is a guaranteed event.
body:
On June 12, two of Bollywood's most polarising figures will go head-to-head at the box office — and this time, the history between them makes the matchup impossible to ignore.

Diljit Dosanjh's **Main Vaapas Aaunga**, directed by Imtiaz Ali and featuring A.R. Rahman's music, will release on the same day as Kangana Ranaut's **Bharat Bhhagya Viddhaata**, a 26/11 drama in which she plays a nurse at Mumbai's Cama Hospital during the terror attacks.

## The Feud That Hasn't Been Forgotten

In December 2020, Dosanjh and Ranaut had one of the most explosive public spats in Indian social media history. The trigger was the farmers' protest. Kangana misidentified an elderly Sikh woman at a protest as a paid actor. Diljit corrected her — publicly, in Punjabi, with a bluntness that made him a folk hero overnight. What followed was days of back-and-forth on Twitter, with Kangana calling him a "Khalistani" sympathiser and Diljit responding in verse-like Punjabi that trended nationally. The exchange ended with Kangana deleting tweets and Diljit earning the lasting respect of the Punjabi diaspora.

Five years later, the feud has cooled — Kangana even said publicly in January 2025 that she had "made peace" with both Diljit and Karan Johar. But the box office doesn't do reconciliation. It does numbers.

## Two Very Different Films

**Main Vaapas Aaunga** is an Imtiaz Ali–A.R. Rahman reunion, their second after the critically acclaimed *Amar Singh Chamkila* on Netflix. The film spans the 1947 Partition era and the present day, starring Vedang Raina, Sharvari, Naseeruddin Shah, and Dosanjh in a role that trades his trademark exuberance for something weightier. For the diaspora — particularly Punjabi families in Canada, the UK, and the US — Partition stories hit differently. This isn't just a film; it's a conversation starter at dinner tables. Imtiaz's track record with diaspora audiences (from *Jab We Met* to *Tamasha* to *Chamkila*) gives the film a built-in overseas constituency.

**Bharat Bhhagya Viddhaata** carries a different kind of weight. Kangana plays one of the nurses who stayed behind at Cama Hospital during 26/11, protecting patients while Leopold Café burned a few hundred metres away. The story is real, the heroism is documented, and the film — presented by PEN Studios and produced by Kangana's Manikarnika Films — is her first release since the underwhelming *Emergency*. The cast includes Girija Oak Godbole, Smita Tambe, and Suhita Thatte, with Manoj Tapadia directing.

## What the Diaspora Will Watch

For NRIs in North America, this isn't a close call in terms of advance buzz. Diljit Dosanjh is a touring phenomenon — his Dil-Luminati world tour sold out arenas across the US, Canada, the UK, and Australia. He performed at Coachella. His face is on billboards in Times Square. In the diaspora market, particularly among Sikh and Punjabi communities, he commands a loyalty that no box-office model can fully capture.

Kangana's audience in the overseas market has been shrinking. *Emergency* underperformed globally, and her political pivot — she is now a sitting BJP Member of Parliament from Mandi — has complicated her positioning as a mainstream actress. The film's patriotic theme may resonate domestically, but diaspora audiences tend to reward storytelling over sentiment.

## The Numbers Game

Both films will also contend with Manoj Bajpayee's *Governor*, a drama about the RBI head who navigated the 1991 economic crisis, and Vikram Bhatt's *Haunted 3D*, which are also eyeing the June 12 window. It's a crowded week.

But the real story isn't about screen count or opening-day occupancy. It's about two people who fought each other on Twitter now fighting for the same audience on the same Friday. The internet remembers everything, and Bollywood forgets nothing.

The only certainty: June 12 will be loud.

*Sources: Bollywood Hungama, SwapUpdate, Zoom TV Entertainment*
